titulo: Forecast says 36°F tonight, so your plants are fine? Not so fast.
receta: regla con numero + debate de una palabra (cover or risk it)
destinatario: se lo manda alguien que tiene huerta o plantas a su amigo que deja la albahaca afuera hasta que se muere
regla_guardable: Forecast low of 36°F or less: cover tender plants with a sheet before sunset, or bring them inside.

interaccion.guardar: Low of 36°F or less: cover tender plants before sunset (bedsheet) or bring them inside.
interaccion.comentar: Do you cover your plants or risk it?

fuentes: NWS Raleigh, Frost/Freeze maps (weather.gov/rah/FrostFreezemaps): frost advisory with forecast lows of 33-36°F and good radiational cooling; offices vary slightly
NWS Tallahassee, Frost and Freeze info (weather.gov/tae/frost_and_freeze_info): frost can form at or near ground level while observed air temperatures are slightly above freezing
University of Illinois Extension, Penn State Extension, University of Minnesota Extension: cover tender plants with an old sheet or light blanket the afternoon before, or move potted plants indoors

frases.texto: The forecast says thirty-six degrees tonight, so your plants are fine.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Many National Weather Service offices issue a frost advisory when lows are forecast between thirty-three and thirty-six degrees on clear, calm nights.
The air near the ground can be colder than the thermometer reading.
So frost can form even when the forecast is above freezing.
Garden experts say to cover tender plants with a bedsheet before sunset, or bring them inside.
Heads up: hardy, established plants usually handle frost fine. It's the tender ones at risk.
Save this: forecast low of thirty-six or less, cover them before sunset.
Do you cover your plants or risk it?
Send this to the friend who leaves their basil outside until it's dead.
